introduction: At the advanced level, examiners test the distinct functional differences between Flywheels and Governors, the classification of Governor sensitivity, and the requirements for dynamic balancing.

core_concepts.title: Flywheel
core_concepts.description:
An energy storage device (reservoir). It controls the fluctuation of speed within a single thermodynamic cycle (engine stroke) by storing energy during the power stroke and releasing it during idle strokes. 
Formula: Maximum fluctuation of energy, Delta_E = I * omega^2 * C_s 
(Where I = moment of inertia, omega = mean angular speed, C_s = coefficient of fluctuation of speed).

core_concepts.title: Governor
core_concepts.description:
A speed-control device that maintains the mean speed of an engine over long periods (multiple cycles) by regulating the supply of working fluid (fuel/steam) when the external load on the engine changes. 
Types: Watt (Pendulum), Porter (Dead-weight), Proell (Dead-weight), and Hartnell (Spring-loaded).

core_concepts.title: Balancing
core_concepts.description:
Unbalanced forces in rotating and reciprocating masses cause severe vibrations. 
1. Static Balancing: The center of gravity must lie exactly on the axis of rotation (Sum of Forces = 0).
2. Dynamic Balancing: There must be no unbalanced centrifugal couples/moments (Sum of Moments = 0). A dynamically balanced system is automatically statically balanced.

important_entities.name: Isochronous Governor
important_entities.significance: A governor is strictly 'Isochronous' if its equilibrium speed is completely constant for all radii of rotation of the flyballs within the working range. Because it operates at only one speed, its sensitiveness is considered infinite.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Most Common Exam Trap: Never confuse their roles! 
- Flywheel: Operates strictly within ONE cycle to smooth out torque delivery. It has zero control over load changes. 
- Governor: Adjusts fuel input over MANY cycles specifically to respond to changes in external load.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Porter is more sensitive than Watt because of the added dead weight, and Proell is more sensitive than Porter because the flyballs are fixed on upward extensions.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent SSC JE Tier-2 theoretical question: 'What is the primary function of a flywheel?' Answer: To limit the fluctuation of speed during a single thermodynamic cycle.
